subject: Request: latency carve-out and committed throughput for Dedicated pool (SkyBridge)
messages:
From: Tara Lim <tara@skybridge.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@skybridge.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool SLA — latency carve-out & throughput ask

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We finished our internal reliability review and a couple of follow-ups came up from the infra team: SkyBridge runs latency-sensitive inference (clinical triage scoring) and wants contractual guarantees around tail latency for a small set of calls. In practice that means:

- A committed slice of the dedicated GPU pool (20 GPUs) with isolation from noisy tenants for the clinical endpoints.
- A guaranteed p95 latency < 180ms for sequences up to 1,024 tokens when routed to the carved-out slice.
- Minimal queueing: requests routed to the slice should not experience queue depth > 5 for steady-state traffic; burst allowance of 3x for short windows.

I realize those are sharp asks — can you tell me whether Redwood can:
1) document a carve-out approach (how routing + queueing will work),
2) provide a short draft SLA for the dedicated slice, and
3) confirm whether there are cost/commitment implications (we expect to sign reserved capacity).

Attaching our reliability checklist and a sample traffic profile. Looking for a go/no-go by Friday if possible.

Thanks,
Tara Lim
VP, Platform Engineering
SkyBridge Health

Attachments: SB_reliability_checklist.csv (csv), traffic_profile_sample.json (json)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Lim <tara@skybridge.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool SLA — latency carve-out & throughput ask

Hi Tara — thank you for the clear breakdown.

Short answer: we can support an isolation carve-out and define a p95 latency commitment for the carved slice, but there are engineering and commercial trade-offs I want to surface before we draft contractual language:

- Isolation model: we can reserve a set of devices inside your Dedicated pool and apply an allocation policy that prefers the slice for routing (soft reserve + strict preferring routing). Full hard isolation (no eviction, absolute single-tenant access) is available for an additional commitment level.
- Queueing behavior: the runtime supports per-slice queue depth caps and priority lanes. For latency-critical traffic we recommend a low queue cap (<=5) and a burst buffer backed by a small warm standby of pre-warmed workers.
- Latency SLOs: we can commit to p95 numbers for the carved slice under an agreed traffic profile. We need to run a deterministic validation window (2–4 weeks) for the exact numbers and to calibrate the headroom.
- Cost/commitment: isolation and warm standby increase reserved capacity and therefore monthly commitment. We can propose a blended reserved SKU with a short ramp (6–12 months).

I will coordinate with Karthik (compute ops) and Jonas (SRE) to put together a short draft SLA and a technical appendix that describes queueing and fallback behavior. Expect a draft by Monday EOD.

Would you prefer the SLA language to define explicit remediation (service credits) for p95 misses vs. a performance-target status page + remediation playbook?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated pool SLA — latency carve-out & throughput ask

Karthik / Jonas — forwarding customer ask. TL;DR: SkyBridge wants a carved-out slice (20 GPUs) with p95 < 180ms for seq<=1024 and queue cap <=5, plus 3x burst. They want draft SLA + cost.

Questions:
1) Karthik — can our allocation policy do a preferential routing that leaves a strict queue cap on the slice and a warm-standby pool for bursts? Do we expose preemptive fallback to a secondary pool if slice is saturated?
2) Jonas — for an SLA with explicit credits (p95 miss), what telemetry/measurement window would be reliable for an enforceable contract? Do we need a blackbox probe or will our internal traces suffice?

I'll bake your answers into the SLA appendix. We should aim to offer two commercial options: (A) soft carve-out + 12-mo reserve (lower commit), (B) hard isolation + 24-mo reserve (higher commit + stricter credits).

Thanks — Hannah

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool SLA — latency carve-out & throughput ask

Hannah / Karthik — quick technical summary and proposed SLA language excerpt for your review. See attached draft PDF (redwood-sla-exception-approval.pdf) and commitment spreadsheet.

Summary:
- Routing/Isolation: implement as a named routing slice with two enforcement modes: 
  * "Preferred" — requests labeled with the SkyBridge routing tag routed to slice where possible; if slice queue depth > cap, request spills to secondary pool (no hard rejection).
  * "Guaranteed" — slice devices are reserved for SkyBridge; no spill unless operator-initiated emergency override. This mode requires minimum 24-month reservation for capacity planning.
- Queueing: we will enforce per-device queue cap and a per-slice queue cap (default 5). Burst handling: a pre-warmed standby of 5 devices provides short-term headroom; sustained bursts are handled by spill to secondary pool or an autoscale action (subject to reserved capacity limits).
- Measurement: p95 and p99 latency will be computed from our edge tracing pipeline. For contractability we recommend a 28-day rolling measurement window with a 99% confidence check. Misses beyond the threshold will trigger service credits defined in the draft.
- Remediation: credits are tiered by severity; we propose small monthly credits for occasional misses and escalation/case review for repeated breaches.

Proposed next steps for commercial:
1) Hannah to send customer draft SLA (attached) + cost table.
2) Customer validates traffic profile in our staging test (we'll run four 2-hour validation runs).
3) After validation, finalize commitment term and sign contract.

I added language that allows a temporary carve-out pilot (8 weeks) with clearly documented measurement windows so customer can validate before long-term commit.

If that looks good I'll prepare the DocuSign-ready SLA and the committed capacity SKU.

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sla-exception-approval.pdf (pdf), dedicated_capacity_commitment.xlsx (xlsx)
